issues.legal_issue: An appeal does not abate in its entirety when a deceased appellant’s interest concerns identifiable property independent of the interests of the other appellants, and the delay in substitution is not excused.
material_facts: A deceased appellant was the donee of specified properties under a separate gift deed, distinct from the properties given to the other donees.
The applications to bring the deceased appellant’s legal representative on record were filed after an unexplained delay of more than twenty-five years.
The decree concerned several reversioners and independent donees with specified interests in identifiable properties.
issues.conclusion: The delay was not condoned, and the appeal abated only in respect of the properties gifted to the deceased appellant, not as a whole.
issues.legal_principle: Where a decree is divisible and the deceased party’s interest relates to specific property independent of the other parties’ interests, the abatement is limited to that interest; an unexplained inordinate delay in seeking substitution need not be condoned.

rule.if: appeal_from_multi_party_decree and decree_is_divisible and deceased_appellant_had_independent_property_interest and substitution_delay_is_unexplained

predicates.appeal_from_multi_party_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree involving multiple parties.
predicates.decree_is_divisible: The decree separates the parties’ interests into identifiable portions that can be dealt with independently.
predicates.deceased_appellant_had_independent_prope: The deceased appellant held an interest in specified property distinct from the interests of the other appellants.
predicates.substitution_delay_is_unexplained: The party seeking substitution does not provide a satisfactory explanation for the substantial delay.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns divisible interests and the deceased appellant’s property interest is independent, an unexplained substitution delay results in abatement only for that appellant’s property.

issues.legal_issue: A widow in possession of inherited property when the Hindu Succession Act came into force became its absolute owner where a mutation entry, without an effective transfer of title, was the basis for the competing claim.
material_facts: A widow inherited land after her husband died without children and was recorded as having transferred it to two minors by mutation, purportedly in accordance with her husband’s wish to adopt them.
The alleged adoption was found not proved in earlier litigation, and the widow continued to live with the minors and manage the property.
The courts below treated the mutation as having divested the widow of title and possession, but the Supreme Court held that the mutation did not convey title or divest her.
The widow was treated as remaining in possession when the Hindu Succession Act came into force and later executed gifts of the land.
Reversioners brought a suit for possession after the widow’s death, challenging the gifts.
issues.conclusion: The widow remained in possession and her limited interest enlarged into absolute ownership when the Hindu Succession Act came into force; she was authorized to deal with the property by gift.
issues.legal_principle: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 enlarged the widow’s limited interest because she continued to possess the property. As held in Smt. Sawarni v. Smt. Inder Kaur, mutation in revenue records neither creates nor extinguishes title and serves the purpose of land-revenue collection. Because the mutation did not transfer title, the widow was not divested of title or possession by it.

rule.if: reversioner_possession_suit and widow_had_limited_inherited_interest and widow_possessed_property_at_succession_change and competing_title_claim_rested_on_mutation and mutation_did_not_transfer_title

predicates.reversioner_possession_suit: The proceeding is a suit by reversioners seeking possession after a widow’s death and challenging her transfer of inherited property.
predicates.widow_had_limited_inherited_interest: A widow held a limited interest in property inherited from her deceased husband.
predicates.widow_possessed_property_at_succession_c: The widow possessed the property when the succession law came into force.
predicates.competing_title_claim_rested_on_mutation: The competing claim that the widow had lost her title relied on a mutation in revenue records.
predicates.mutation_did_not_transfer_title: The mutation was not an effective transfer of ownership of the property.

issues.definition: If reversioners seek possession after a widow’s death, and she possessed inherited property when succession law changed while the competing claim rests only on a non-transferring mutation, she becomes its absolute owner and may transfer it.

issues.legal_issue: A prior decree declaring only that a mutation would not affect reversionary rights does not itself transfer title to the reversioners or bar their later possession claim as res judicata.
material_facts: In an earlier suit, a reversioner sought a declaration that a mutation described as a gift would not affect reversionary rights after the widow’s death or remarriage.
The earlier decree was affirmed on appeal and was relied on by the reversioners in their later suit for possession.
The mutation did not convey title, and the earlier suit had sought only a declaration concerning its effect on reversionary rights.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming the earlier decree operated as res judicata, it did not assist the reversioners in the later suit because it neither conveyed title to them nor decided a claim to title based on an effective transfer.
issues.legal_principle: A decree’s effect is confined to the relief and matter it decided. The earlier declaratory proceeding concerned whether the mutation affected reversionary rights; since mutation does not convey or extinguish title, that decree did not vest title in the reversioners.

rule.if: later_reversioner_possession_suit and prior_decree_was_declaratory_only and prior_decree_addressed_mutation_effect and mutation_did_not_transfer_title

predicates.later_reversioner_possession_suit: The proceeding is a later suit by reversioners seeking possession of inherited property.
predicates.prior_decree_was_declaratory_only: The earlier proceeding sought and granted declaratory relief rather than a transfer of ownership.
predicates.prior_decree_addressed_mutation_effect: The earlier decree addressed whether a mutation affected reversionary rights.
predicates.mutation_did_not_transfer_title: The mutation did not convey ownership of the property.

issues.definition: A prior declaration about the effect of a non-title-transferring mutation does not bar a later reversioner’s possession claim because the earlier decree did not itself vest title.

issues.legal_issue: A revenue mutation entry is to be treated as correct unless the contrary is established, and an unchallenged entry cannot simply be disregarded.
material_facts: The trial court accepted one mutation entry as conveying title but doubted a later mutation entry in the widow’s favour.
The later entry had remained unchallenged, and the trial court placed on the appellants the burden of proving the entries correct.
The Supreme Court held that the trial court had not applied a consistent standard to the entries.
issues.conclusion: Mutation entries must be taken as correct unless the contrary is established, and the unchallenged later entry could not be ignored, although mutation entries do not themselves convey title.
issues.legal_principle: Gurbaksh Singh v. Nikka Singh holds that mutation entries must be taken as correct unless the contrary is established. An affected person must challenge an entry through the procedure provided by law; an unchallenged entry cannot be brushed aside. This evidentiary effect does not make mutation an instrument that creates or extinguishes title.

rule.if: dispute_involves_revenue_entries and revenue_entry_exists and contrary_to_entry_is_not_established and entry_remains_unchallenged

predicates.dispute_involves_revenue_entries: The proceeding involves a dispute about entries in revenue records.
predicates.revenue_entry_exists: A mutation entry concerning the property has been made in the revenue records.
predicates.contrary_to_entry_is_not_established: No evidence establishes that the entry is incorrect.
predicates.entry_remains_unchallenged: A person affected by the entry has not challenged it through the available legal procedure.

issues.definition: When a revenue entry exists and remains unchallenged without evidence showing it to be incorrect, it is treated as correct, though it does not establish title.
